facts.statement: The holotype of Eotrachodon consists of a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton found in Alabama.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in the Mooreville Chalk Formation (Upper Santonian) of Alabama in 2007 and includes a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton

facts.statement: Eotrachodon was a relatively small dinosaur with a body length of about 5 meters.
facts.quote: Eotrachodon es bastante pequeño, con una longitud corporal de unos 5 metros

facts.statement: The lateral projection of the praemaxilla curves downward at an angle of 165 degrees relative to the longitudinal axis of the nasal cavity opening.
facts.quote: La proyección lateral de la praemaxilla se curva repentinamente hacia abajo, formando un ángulo de 165 ° con el eje longitudinal del hueco alrededor de la abertura de la nariz

facts.statement: The lower sleep window is large, being both taller and wider than the eye socket.
facts.quote: La ventana inferior para dormir es grande, más alta y más ancha que la cuenca del ojo

facts.statement: The holotype fossil MSC 7949 was discovered in 2007 in the Upper Santonian layer of the Mooreville Chalk Formation, dating to approximately 84 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil , holotipo MSC 7949, se encontró en 2007 en una capa de la Formación Mooreville Chalk que data del último Santoniano, de aproximadamente 84 millones de años

facts.statement: The species Eotrachodon orientalis was named and described in 2016 by Albert Prieto-Márquez, Gregory M. Erickson, and Jun A. Ebersole.
facts.quote: En 2016, el tipo de Eotrachodon orientalis fue nombrado y descrito por Albert Prieto-Márquez , Gregory M. Erickson y Jun A. Ebersole

facts.statement: Eotrachodon lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago in the Santonian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83 millones de años durante el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: The fossil record for Eotrachodon spans from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Eotrachodon was established by Prieto-Márquez, Erickson, and Ebersole in 2016.
Eotrachodon is classified within the dinosaur family Hadrosauridae.
The skull possesses a derived nasal bone structure that may be a precursor to the form seen in Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene una estructura derivada libremente del hueso nasal que podría ser un precursor de la forma de Saurolophinae

facts.statement: The discovery of Eotrachodon suggests that the typical nasal structure of saurolophines developed early, shortly after their divergence from lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Eotrachodon indica que la estructura típica de la nariz de las saurolofininidos se desarrolló temprano, justo después de la división con los lambeosaurinidos

facts.statement: Eotrachodon holds the distinction of being the first known hadrosaurid skull discovered in Appalachia.
facts.quote: Este es el primer cráneo de un miembro de los Hadrosauridae conocido de Appalachia

facts.statement: In phylogenetic analysis, Eotrachodon is placed as a basal member of Hadrosauridae, positioned above Hadrosaurus and as the sister taxon to Saurolophidae.
facts.quote: Eotrachodon se coloca basal en Hadrosauridae , sobre Hadrosaurus , como la especie hermana de Saurolophidae

facts.statement: There is a taxonomic debate regarding the classification of this lineage, with some researchers using the term Saurolophidae while others refer to it as Euhadrosauria.
facts.quote: El término "Saurolophidae" caracteriza la taxonomía de Prieto-Márquez, otros investigadores a veces llaman a esta rama la Euhadrosauria
